mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both housing starts and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative outlook for corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between the joint decline of HOUST and RSAFS and negative 60-day SPX returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO), manufacturing output contraction reduces corporate profit margins and future earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (measured by the change in retail sales, RSAFS) over the past month indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI exceeds 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both employment growth (PAYEMS) and a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a severe labor market slowdown that reduces household income and consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not predict negative 20-day SPX returns with a Rank IC > 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-rate environment (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) with accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.0%), the market anticipates imminent monetary tightening, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition (FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.0%).
